task.description:
Validate the CODE-DESIGNER Step 01 design for PAR-01, PAR-02, PAR-03, PAR-04 (events table monthly range partitioning -- high risk, core table). Standard checks apply (every AC traced, no implementation code, tools/lint_design_artefact.py clean). CRITICAL ADDITIONAL CHECK: both PAR-01 and PAR-03 design docs flag that src/event_store/store.zig::Store.archive() currently issues DELETE FROM events / DELETE FROM events_archive-adjacent statements that become actively incompatible with PAR-03's own AC ("No DELETE statement SHALL run against events or events_archive at any point") the moment PAR-03 ships. Both docs recommend deferring archive()'s retirement/rewrite as a follow-up rather than fixing it in this batch, reasoning that PAR-01's ACs don't mention archive() and PAR-03's ACs govern the NEW retention mechanism, not the old one. Assess this reasoning carefully: does PAR-03's AC ("No DELETE... at any point") actually mean literally zero DELETE statements can exist in the codebase touching these tables once PAR-03 ships (in which case archive() being left as-is would make this batch's own release FALSELY claim AC compliance, since archive() would still be callable and would still violate it), or does it mean PAR-03's OWN mechanism specifically never deletes (a narrower, correct-as-designed reading)? This determines whether deferring archive() is safe or is a hidden AC violation. If genuinely ambiguous, this may need to route to REQ-ANALYST rather than being decided unilaterally by either CODE-DESIGNER or you.

RE-VALIDATION (after REWORK 1): CODE-DESIGNER added the RetentionClassForbidden guard (app-level in Registry.registerType() + a DB-level CHECK constraint backstop) and specified FULL REMOVAL of Store.archive() (confirmed zero src/ call sites), since it drives 4 traced test cases for ES-07 (SHOULD, RELEASED) and ADP-11 (MUST, RELEASED) -- TC-ES-07-01, TC-ES-07-02, TC-ADP-11-02, TC-ADP-11-03. The design specifies these 4 tests be REWRITTEN to assert archive() is retired and repointed at PAR-03's own new PartitionRetention mechanism, in the SAME batch/commit. CRITICAL RE-VALIDATION FOCUS: does this design genuinely keep ES-07 and ADP-11 (both already-RELEASED requirements) satisfied after the rewrite, or does retiring archive() risk silently regressing a released requirement's actual guaranteed behavior? Read ES-07 and ADP-11's full requirement bodies and their existing (soon-to-be-rewritten) AC mappings in tests/specs/ES-07.md and tests/specs/ADP-11.md (if they exist) before judging this. This is the single most important thing to verify in this re-validation -- a design that retires code satisfying one requirement in order to satisfy a different requirement's AC, without genuinely proving the first requirement still holds, would be trading one compliance gap for another.

RE-VALIDATION (after REWORK 2 -- this is the SECOND rework cycle on this handoff, of max 3; be thorough, this is likely the last chance before escalation if it fails again). CODE-DESIGNER added append-time retention-class routing to Store.append() (a new getType() call determining events vs events_ephemeral as INSERT target), widened PAR-02's partition-maintenance loop to also provision events_ephemeral partitions, and specified TC-ADP-11-02 can now be grounded in real routing + real ephemeral-drop behavior end to end. Re-verify all of this independently: read the updated par-03 and par-02 design docs, confirm the routing design is sound (does it genuinely not break the existing, released ES-05 validatePayload() interface as claimed -- check the one external call site), confirm events_ephemeral now genuinely gets partitions provisioned (not just events), and confirm TC-ADP-11-02's rewrite plan is now concretely groundable. Also re-check the original PAR-01..04 AC coverage and RetentionClassForbidden guard from rework 1 are unaffected. If you find yet another gap, treat this as potentially needing escalation guidance from ORCH given rework budget -- report FAIL with full clarity if so, do not force a PASS.
acceptance_criteria: Every AC in PAR-01, PAR-02, PAR-03, PAR-04 traced to a design section
No implementation code in the design
Migration approach correctly scoped as fresh-schema-only (not attempting PAR-05's online conversion)
Current events/events_archive shape preservation verified against actual migration history

Store.archive() vs PAR-03 DELETE-prohibition conflict explicitly resolved: either confirmed genuinely non-blocking with sound reasoning, or flagged as requiring REQ-ANALYST clarification before BACKEND-DEV proceeds

result.summary: Rework 2 re-validated and PASSES. Independently re-verified all 5 focus points against actual source, not design-doc claims. (1) validatePayload() interface genuinely untouched: grep confirms exactly one external call site (store.zig:262); design instead threads retention_class through a second registry.getType() call (store.zig, after line 267, still pre-BEGIN). EventTypeRecord{} is constructed in exactly 2 places in registry.zig (registerType() placeholder, getType() real parse) and getType()'s one external caller (instances.zig:896) only reads a success/error signal and immediately calls freeTypeRecord() -- confirmed by reading that call site in full. freeTypeRecord() currently frees exactly 3 fields (name/json_schema/description), matching the design's claimed baseline before adding a 4th (retention_class). Claim accurate. (2) events_ephemeral partition provisioning confirmed genuinely wired: par-02-partition-maintenance-job.md's runMaintenanceCycle() body sketch step 2 and Data flow diagram both now iterate parent in ["events", "events_ephemeral"], not events alone; Open questions #4 marks this RESOLVED with correct cross-reference to par-03's REWORK 2 section. Not a claim without substance -- the loop body, the CREATE TABLE templating, and the attachPartitionTimed() call are all shown widened. (3) TC-ADP-11-02 rewrite is concretely groundable: traced the full chain -- WIDGET_CREATED (non-protected) registered with retention_class=delete passes REWORK 1's RetentionClassForbidden guard (does not match {INSTANCE_,TASK_,GATEWAY_,EXECUTION_}* prefixes) -> Store.append() -> getType() reads retention_class=delete -> target_table=events_ephemeral -> INSERT lands in events_ephemeral (a real partitioned table that now gets partitions via fix (2)) -> PartitionRetention.runEphemeralDrop() queries plat_partition_catalog for parent_table=events_ephemeral rows and can find/guard/drop the row. No remaining gap in this chain -- confirmed by reading store.zig::append(), registry.zig::getType(), and PAR-04's attachPartitionTimed()/verifyAttachConstraints() (unchanged, correctly depended upon). (4) Rework 1's RetentionClassForbidden guard (Zig-side validateRegisterParams + DB-level chk_retention_class_protected_family CHECK) is untouched by rework 2 and remains intact; isProtectedEventFamily/ProtectedFamilyHardDeleteForbidden in store.zig (ADP-11, pre-existing) confirmed still present and unaffected. PAR-01/02/03/04 AC coverage spot-checked against docs/requirements.yaml verbatim bodies -- notably PAR-03's own requirement prose already names events_ephemeral and "the type never routes to events_ephemeral" (AC1), confirming the routing mechanism this rework adds is not an invention but closes a gap between the requirement text and the prior design's silence on the mechanism. Store.archive() confirmed still present at store.zig:947 (expected -- removal is BACKEND-DEV Step 2a scope per this design, not yet executed). (5) All 4 design docs (par-01, par-02, par-03, par-04) pass tools/lint_design_artefact.py with 0 issues. Both Type C migration YAMLs (par-02-partition-catalog, par-03-retention-class) pass lint and tools/codegen_migration.py --dry-run exits 0 for both, with generated SQL/test previews covering their codegen-scoped acceptance criteria (events_ephemeral's hand-written CREATE TABLE is correctly excluded from the YAML per the already-resolved Y125 composite-PK constraint, documented in both the YAML header and design Open questions #2). No new gap of comparable severity found. This rework genuinely closes the gap identified in rework 1's FAIL -- not a placeholder or a claim without mechanism.
